clue.text: Run off some jazz

definitions.meaning: to run off is to leave in a hurry, as when telling a cat to clear off
a style of wordless improvised jazz singing

explanation.surface: An instruction to dash away from a jazz performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: an imperative to go away, and nonsense-syllable jazz vocalising.

clue.text: Idiot, daily, to tell stories

parts.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day

explanation.surface: Calling a cleaner a fool for spinning yarns.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' or CHAR is British slang for a cleaner who comes in to clean houses.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a fool, as in feeling a right one.

clue.text: Brown bread for your health, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: sliced bread browned under a grill
a raised glass and a wish for someone's health, a drinking salute

explanation.surface: Wholemeal loaves recommended for being good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown bread' reads as wholemeal; here 'Brown' is a verb, to grill bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Grilled bread slices, and a salute drunk to someone's good health, as in raising glasses.

clue.text: Strength of character in personal column

definitions.meaning: firmness and resolve in a person
a person's own column, the spine running down the back

explanation.surface: A newspaper's personal ads section showing moral fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal column' looks like the lonely-hearts page of a paper; here it is the vertebral column every person has.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve is figuratively called this, and literally it is the spinal column, a body's own column.

clue.text: Extra farewell

definitions.meaning: in cricket a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball, one of the extras

explanation.surface: An additional goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a run scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched counts as an extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket run awarded without a hit, and a casual parting word.

clue.text: Boundary between land and water so clean, it turns out

indicators.note: turns out suggests something revealed in a new form, so the letters of so clean, it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy beach is revealed where shore meets sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The outline of a land mass along the sea, the shore's edge.

clue.text: In time, metal put in sack

definitions.note: adjective: in cricket the side that is in is at the crease

indicators.note: put in places the time and metal letters inside the container word

explanation.surface: Instructions for loading something metal into a sack in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but it is the definition: in cricket the team that is 'in' is the side at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the team taking its turn at the crease is described as being in.

clue.text: Rope, feature including loop?

indicators.note: including puts the round letter inside the facial word

parts.note: the nose is a facial feature
O is shaped like a loop

explanation.surface: A rope whose distinguishing feature is a loop, as in a lasso.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of rope with a running knot, for hanging or snaring, so a type of rope.

clue.text: US city partially waned, as apparently backwards

indicators.note: the run of letters taken from inside the phrase is then read in the opposite direction
only part of the words waned, as apparently is used, so a run of letters sits inside them

explanation.surface: A remark that some American city has declined, seemingly in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' picks ANEDASAP out of 'waned, as apparently' and 'backwards' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Californian city near Los Angeles, home of the Rose Bowl, so a US municipality.

clue.text: Implement — also utensil ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word utensil

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget described as both an implement and a utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is any instrument or device used for a job, a close synonym.

clue.text: Secret plan to take cannabis around Lithuanian capital

indicators.note: the drug word goes around the letter taken from the nationality
capital here means the initial or head letter of Lithuanian, not the city of Vilnius

explanation.surface: A drug-smuggling scheme in Vilnius, the capital of Lithuania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lithuanian capital' tempts towards Vilnius; it means just the capital letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy or covert scheme is a synonym, as in a plot to overthrow the king.

clue.text: Comprehensive back in action

indicators.note: in places the rear-end word inside the word for an act

parts.note: a deed is an action or act
the tail is the back or rear end

explanation.surface: A sports report: an all-round player returning to the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough account covering every point is full of particulars, hence a synonym.

clue.text: Awfully smart idea to adapt for the theatre

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of smart idea are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Mocking a clever notion to turn something into a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn a novel or story into a stage play is to put it into theatrical form.

clue.text: Praise cultivated in land of old

indicators.note: cultivated soil is turned over and worked, so the letters of Praise are reworked

explanation.surface: Acclaim grown in an ancient realm, as if farming flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical name of the country now called Iran, so an ancient land.

clue.text: Southern people embraced by an Arab

indicators.note: embraced by means the word for people goes inside the letters of an

explanation.surface: A southern tribe welcomed by an Arab host.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval European term for an Arab or Muslim, especially in the Crusades.

clue.text: , Eat as a joke audibly?

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the phrase for joking is said out loud

parts.note: doing something as a joke is doing it in jest

explanation.surface: A query whether one consumes food purely for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: To take food or drink into the body by swallowing, a formal synonym for consuming.

clue.text: Part one, it's rearranged to cover first of chapters

indicators.note: the jumbled letters cover, or enclose, the single opening letter
rearranged plainly signals the letters of one, it's going into a new order
first of takes the opening letter of chapters

explanation.surface: An editor reorganising part one of a book to take in the opening chapters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' makes SETION from ONE IT'S, and 'to cover' puts the C from 'first of chapters' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion or division of a whole, such as a segment of a text.

clue.text: New menus are identifying what to type to log in?

definitions.text: what to type to log in?

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh version, so the letters of menus are are made over

explanation.surface: Fresh computer menus showing the login field to fill in.
explanation.definitionFit: A login prompt asks for an account's identifier, typed alongside the password.

clue.text: Malingerer denied victory, one going downhill

indicators.note: denied means the shirker word loses the victory letter

parts.note: a skiver is British slang for one shirking work

explanation.surface: A shirker missing out on a win and so heading downhill in life.
explanation.walkthrough: A SKIVER is British slang for someone who dodges work or school.
explanation.definitionFit: A downhill slope racer on snow is literally someone travelling downhill.

clue.text: Vermin taking a thousand diamonds

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Rodents running off with a great hoard of gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Small rodents that infest houses are classic pests, plural to match the plural noun.

clue.text: Parent kept under wraps

definitions.meaning: British informal word for a mother
an embalmed body wrapped in bandages, as in ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: A secretive parent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept under wraps' suggests secrecy; literally it is a body wound in linen bandages.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother informally in Britain, and an embalmed Egyptian corpse literally wrapped up.

clue.text: Plate found in cupboard is charming

indicators.note: found in tells the solver the letters are sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A lovely dish discovered in a charming cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat round object, a dish or plate, as in a flat circular piece.

clue.text: Difficulty sleeping in higgledy-piggledy mansion one tucked in

indicators.note: tucked in places the numeral inside the jumbled house letters
higgledy-piggledy means in confused disorder, so the letters of mansion are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone unable to sleep in a messy house with one person snuggled in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'higgledy-piggledy' turns MANSION into INSOMNA, and 'tucked in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronic inability to fall or stay asleep is the medical name for sleeplessness.

clue.text: Remain, having cleared out a filthy home

indicators.note: having cleared out means the letter a is removed from the word for remain

explanation.surface: Someone told to stay put after clearing a dirty house.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig's pen, and by extension any very dirty dwelling.

clue.text: Very large royal

definitions.meaning: a sum that is lavish or generous, as in a handsome amount
befitting or belonging to a monarch's son

explanation.surface: A description of an enormous member of the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: It means generous or sumptuous, and literally relating to a royal heir like a prince.

clue.text: American tug

definitions.meaning: informal word for someone from the United States

explanation.surface: A US citizen giving something a pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a person from the USA, and also a sudden hard pull on something.
